[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘賣命]]| 社格=[[元伊勢]]
[[県社]]| 創建=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]8年| 本殿=[[神明造]]| 例祭=[[5月1日]]| 神事=}} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]][[近江町]]に鎮座する[[神社]]である。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]] *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘賣命]] ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 元伊勢のひとつ。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]『[[倭姫命]]世記』によると、伊勢の大神が[[垂仁天皇]]8年（紀元前1世紀）に「甲可日雲宮（現在の甲賀市[[日雲神社]]）」から遷り、2年間本神社の地に留まった[[元伊勢]]と伝わっている。'''坂田宮'''とも称した。[[享保]]18年（1733年）に時の彦根藩主[[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受け社頭が整備されて以降、彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。[[明治]]14年（1881年）に[[郷社]]、[[昭和]]20年（1945年）に県社に列格した。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮 ** 四所宮 ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 関連項目 == *[[神道]] *[[神社]] *[[元伊勢]] {{神道 横}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:米原市]] [[Category:府県社]]

{{神社 |名称 = 坂田神明宮 |画像 = |所在地 = [[滋賀県]][[米原市]][[近江町]]宇賀野835-2 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|scale:25000}} |祭神 = [[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮）
[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社） |社格 = 式内小社論社（岡神社）・旧県社 |創建 = 伝垂仁天皇8年 |本殿 = [[神明造]]（両宮とも） |別名 = 坂田宮 |札所等 = 元伊勢 |例祭 = [[5月1日]] |神事 = }} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]][[近江町]]に鎮座する[[神社]]（[[神明神社]]）である。[[元伊勢]]の伝承地である'''坂田宮'''（内宮）と、[[式内社論社]]である'''岡神社'''（外宮）の両宮からなる。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮、内宮） *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社、外宮） ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 坂田宮は古くから「坂田大神宮」とも称し、[[近江国]][[坂田郡]]の[[総社]]として信仰を集めた。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]である『[[倭姫命世記]]』によると、天皇の命を受けて伊勢の大神（天照皇大神）の鎮座地を求めた[[倭姫命]]は[[垂仁天皇]]8年に「甲可日雲宮（こうがのひくものみや）現[[甲賀市]]の[[日雲神社]]他、伝承地多数。」から「坂田宮」に遷り、2年間奉斎したとあるが、社伝にその「坂田宮」の跡地に命の徳を偲んで祀ったのが坂田宮の起源であるという。元伊勢の伝承地であるが、また当地は[[伊勢神宮]]の[[御厨]]であった[[坂田御厨]]が置かれた地でもあり、その起源は倭姫命が来た時に献上された[[神田]]にあるという『伊勢の神宮』。。 岡神社は近世には「'''岡天王社'''」「'''若宮'''」と称されていた[[出口延経]]『[[神名帳考証]]』。。社伝によれば、[[孝安天皇]]の時代に宇賀野魂命（うかのみたまのみこと。その別称が豊受毘売命）が降臨し、時を同じくして筑摩村に[[御食津神|御食都神（みけつかみ）]]、岩脇村に[[大歳神]]が降臨、この3神を合わせて「筑摩三所の神」と称したといい筑摩神は現[[筑摩神社 (米原市)|筑摩神社]]、岩脇神は現[[稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)|稲荷神社]]。、また鎮座地「宇賀野」は「宇賀野魂」という神名に因んだものであるという『近江坂田郡志』、滋賀県坂田郡役所、大正2年。。その後、[[延喜式神名帳|延喜の制]]で近江国の小社（国幣小社）に列した坂田郡「岡神社」であるとされ岡神社の論社も複数存在するが、明治の『特選神名牒』は当地にを古く岡村という村があった事、「岡」の音は「宇賀」や「受（うけ）」に通う事を徴として当神社を比定する。、後に坂田宮に[[合祀]]されたものであるという『式内社調査報告』所引『明治神社誌料』。。 後に[[建武]]の兵乱で兵火に罹ったために[[佐々木秀綱]]によって再建されたものの、[[応仁の乱]]以降も再々兵燹に遭ったために漸次荒廃していったが、[[享保]]18年（[[1733年]]）に時の[[彦根藩|彦根藩主]][[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受けて再興、社頭も整備されて以降、「坂田神明宮」と称して彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。 [[明治]]14年（[[1881年]]）2月1日に[[郷社]]に列し、同41年4月29日に[[神饌幣帛料供進社]]に指定、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）には[[県社]]に昇格した。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#別宮|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:式内小社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:府県社]] [[Category:米原市]]

[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社） |社格 = 式内小社論社（岡神社）・旧県社 |創建 = 伝垂仁天皇8年 |本殿 = [[神明造]]（両宮とも） |別名 = 坂田宮 |札所等 = 元伊勢 |例祭 = [[5月1日]] |神事 = }} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]][[近江町]]に鎮座する[[神社]]（[[神明神社]]）である。[[元伊勢]]の伝承地である'''坂田宮'''（内宮）と、[[式内社論社]]である'''岡神社'''（外宮）の両宮からなる。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮、内宮） *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社、外宮） ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 坂田宮は古くから「坂田大神宮」とも称し、[[近江国]][[坂田郡]]の[[総社]]として信仰を集めた。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]である『[[倭姫命世記]]』によると、天皇の命を受けて伊勢の大神（天照皇大神）の鎮座地を求めた[[倭姫命]]は[[垂仁天皇]]8年に「甲可日雲宮（こうがのひくものみや）現[[甲賀市]]の[[日雲神社]]他、伝承地多数。」から「坂田宮」に遷り、2年間奉斎したとあるが、社伝にその「坂田宮」の跡地に命の徳を偲んで祀ったのが坂田宮の起源であるという。元伊勢の伝承地であるが、また当地は[[伊勢神宮]]の[[御厨]]であった[[坂田御厨]]が置かれた地でもあり、その起源は倭姫命が来た時に献上された[[神田]]にあるという『伊勢の神宮』。。 岡神社は近世には「'''岡天王社'''」「'''若宮'''」と称されていた[[出口延経]]『[[神名帳考証]]』。。社伝によれば、[[孝安天皇]]の時代に宇賀野魂命（うかのみたまのみこと。その別称が豊受毘売命）が降臨し、時を同じくして筑摩村に[[御食津神|御食都神（みけつかみ）]]、岩脇村に[[大歳神]]が降臨、この3神を合わせて「筑摩三所の神」と称したといい筑摩神は現[[筑摩神社 (米原市)|筑摩神社]]、岩脇神は現[[稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)|稲荷神社]]。、また鎮座地「宇賀野」は「宇賀野魂」という神名に因んだものであるという『近江坂田郡志』、滋賀県坂田郡役所、大正2年。。その後、[[延喜式神名帳|延喜の制]]で近江国の小社（国幣小社）に列した坂田郡「岡神社」であるとされ岡神社の論社も複数存在するが、明治の『特選神名牒』は当地にを古く岡村という村があった事、「岡」の音は「宇賀」や「受（うけ）」に通う事を徴として当神社を比定する。、後に坂田宮に[[合祀]]されたものであるという『式内社調査報告』所引『明治神社誌料』。。 後に[[建武 (日本)|建武]]の兵乱で兵火に罹ったために[[佐々木秀綱]]によって再建されたものの、[[応仁の乱]]以降も再々兵燹に遭ったために漸次荒廃していったが、[[享保]]18年（[[1733年]]）に時の[[彦根藩|彦根藩主]][[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受けて再興、社頭も整備されて以降、「坂田神明宮」と称して彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。 [[明治]]14年（[[1881年]]）2月1日に[[郷社]]に列し、同41年4月29日に[[神饌幣帛料供進社]]に指定、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）には[[県社]]に昇格した。 ==祭事== 例祭 - [[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社） |社格 = 式内小社論社（岡神社）・旧県社 |創建 = 伝垂仁天皇8年 |本殿 = [[神明造]]（両宮とも） |別名 = 坂田宮 |札所等 = 元伊勢 |例祭 = [[5月1日]] |神事 = }} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]][[近江町]]に鎮座する[[神社]]（[[神明神社]]）である。[[元伊勢]]の伝承地である'''坂田宮'''（内宮）と、[[式内社論社]]である'''岡神社'''（外宮）の両宮からなる。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮、内宮） *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社、外宮） ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 坂田宮は古くから「坂田大神宮」とも称し、[[近江国]][[坂田郡]]の[[総社]]として信仰を集めた。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]である『[[倭姫命世記]]』によると、天皇の命を受けて伊勢の大神（天照皇大神）の鎮座地を求めた[[倭姫命]]は[[垂仁天皇]]8年に「甲可日雲宮（こうがのひくものみや）現[[甲賀市]]の[[日雲神社]]他、伝承地多数。」から「坂田宮」に遷り、2年間奉斎したとあるが、社伝にその「坂田宮」の跡地に命の徳を偲んで祀ったのが坂田宮の起源であるという。元伊勢の伝承地であるが、また当地は[[伊勢神宮]]の[[御厨]]であった[[坂田御厨]]が置かれた地でもあり、その起源は倭姫命が来た時に献上された[[神田]]にあるという『伊勢の神宮』。。 岡神社は近世には「'''岡天王社'''」「'''若宮'''」と称されていた[[出口延経]]『[[神名帳考証]]』。。社伝によれば、[[孝安天皇]]の時代に宇賀野魂命（うかのみたまのみこと。その別称が豊受毘売命）が降臨し、時を同じくして筑摩村に[[御食津神|御食都神（みけつかみ）]]、岩脇村に[[大歳神]]が降臨、この3神を合わせて「筑摩三所の神」と称したといい筑摩神は現[[筑摩神社 (米原市)|筑摩神社]]、岩脇神は現[[稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)|稲荷神社]]。、また鎮座地「宇賀野」は「宇賀野魂」という神名に因んだものであるという『近江坂田郡志』、滋賀県坂田郡役所、大正2年。。その後、[[延喜式神名帳|延喜の制]]で近江国の小社（国幣小社）に列した坂田郡「岡神社」であるとされ岡神社の論社も複数存在するが、明治の『特選神名牒』は当地にを古く岡村という村があった事、「岡」の音は「宇賀」や「受（うけ）」に通う事を徴として当神社を比定する。、後に坂田宮に[[合祀]]されたものであるという『式内社調査報告』所引『明治神社誌料』。。 後に[[建武 (日本)|建武]]の兵乱で兵火に罹ったために[[佐々木秀綱]]によって再建されたものの、[[応仁の乱]]以降も再々兵燹に遭ったために漸次荒廃していったが、[[享保]]18年（[[1733年]]）に時の[[彦根藩|彦根藩主]][[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受けて再興、社頭も整備されて以降、「坂田神明宮」と称して彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。 [[明治]]14年（[[1881年]]）2月1日に[[郷社]]に列し、同41年4月29日に[[神饌幣帛料供進社]]に指定、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）には[[県社]]に昇格した。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#別宮|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:近江国の式内社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:滋賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:米原市]]

[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社） |社格 = 式内小社論社（岡神社）・旧県社 |創建 = 伝垂仁天皇8年 |本殿 = [[神明造]]（両宮とも） |別名 = 坂田宮 |札所等 = 元伊勢 |例祭 = [[5月1日]] |神事 = }} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]]宇賀野に鎮座する[[神社]]（[[神明神社]]）である。[[元伊勢]]の伝承地である'''坂田宮'''（内宮）と、[[式内社論社]]である'''岡神社'''（外宮）の両宮からなる。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮、内宮） *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社、外宮） ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 坂田宮は古くから「坂田大神宮」とも称し、[[近江国]][[坂田郡]]の[[総社]]として信仰を集めた。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]である『[[倭姫命世記]]』によると、天皇の命を受けて伊勢の大神（天照皇大神）の鎮座地を求めた[[倭姫命]]は[[垂仁天皇]]8年に「甲可日雲宮（こうがのひくものみや）現[[甲賀市]]の[[日雲神社]]他、伝承地多数。」から「坂田宮」に遷り、2年間奉斎したとあるが、社伝にその「坂田宮」の跡地に命の徳を偲んで祀ったのが坂田宮の起源であるという。元伊勢の伝承地であるが、また当地は[[伊勢神宮]]の[[御厨]]であった[[坂田御厨]]が置かれた地でもあり、その起源は倭姫命が来た時に献上された[[神田]]にあるという『伊勢の神宮』。。 岡神社は近世には「'''岡天王社'''」「'''若宮'''」と称されていた[[出口延経]]『[[神名帳考証]]』。。社伝によれば、[[孝安天皇]]の時代に宇賀野魂命（うかのみたまのみこと。その別称が豊受毘売命）が降臨し、時を同じくして筑摩村に[[御食津神|御食都神（みけつかみ）]]、岩脇村に[[大歳神]]が降臨、この3神を合わせて「筑摩三所の神」と称したといい筑摩神は現[[筑摩神社 (米原市)|筑摩神社]]、岩脇神は現[[稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)|稲荷神社]]。、また鎮座地「宇賀野」は「宇賀野魂」という神名に因んだものであるという『近江坂田郡志』、滋賀県坂田郡役所、大正2年。。その後、[[延喜式神名帳|延喜の制]]で近江国の小社（国幣小社）に列した坂田郡「岡神社」であるとされ岡神社の論社も複数存在するが、明治の『特選神名牒』は当地にを古く岡村という村があった事、「岡」の音は「宇賀」や「受（うけ）」に通う事を徴として当神社を比定する。、後に坂田宮に[[合祀]]されたものであるという『式内社調査報告』所引『明治神社誌料』。。 後に[[建武 (日本)|建武]]の兵乱で兵火に罹ったために[[佐々木秀綱]]によって再建されたものの、[[応仁の乱]]以降も再々兵燹に遭ったために漸次荒廃していったが、[[享保]]18年（[[1733年]]）に時の[[彦根藩|彦根藩主]][[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受けて再興、社頭も整備されて以降、「坂田神明宮」と称して彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。 [[明治]]14年（[[1881年]]）2月1日に[[郷社]]に列し、同41年4月29日に[[神饌幣帛料供進社]]に指定、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）には[[県社]]に昇格した。 ==祭事== 例祭 - [[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社） |社格 = 式内小社論社（岡神社）・旧県社 |創建 = 伝垂仁天皇8年 |本殿 = [[神明造]]（両宮とも） |別名 = 坂田宮 |札所等 = 元伊勢 |例祭 = [[5月1日]] |神事 = }} '''坂田神明宮'''（さかたしんめいぐう）は[[滋賀県]][[米原市]]宇賀野に鎮座する[[神社]]（[[神明神社]]）である。[[元伊勢]]の伝承地である'''坂田宮'''（内宮）と、[[式内社論社]]である'''岡神社'''（外宮）の両宮からなる。 ==祭神== *[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]（坂田宮、内宮） *[[トヨウケビメ|豊受毘売命]]（岡神社、外宮） ==神紋== 丸に橘 ==歴史== 坂田宮は古くから「坂田大神宮」とも称し、[[近江国]][[坂田郡]]の[[総社]]として信仰を集めた。[[神道五部書|伊勢神道五部書]]である『[[倭姫命世記]]』によると、天皇の命を受けて伊勢の大神（天照皇大神）の鎮座地を求めた[[倭姫命]]は[[垂仁天皇]]8年に「甲可日雲宮（こうがのひくものみや）現[[甲賀市]]の[[日雲神社]]他、伝承地多数。」から「坂田宮」に遷り、2年間奉斎したとあるが、社伝にその「坂田宮」の跡地に命の徳を偲んで祀ったのが坂田宮の起源であるという。元伊勢の伝承地であるが、また当地は[[伊勢神宮]]の[[御厨]]であった[[坂田御厨]]が置かれた地でもあり、その起源は倭姫命が来た時に献上された[[神田]]にあるという『伊勢の神宮』。。 岡神社は近世には「'''岡天王社'''」「'''若宮'''」と称されていた[[出口延経]]『[[神名帳考証]]』。。社伝によれば、[[孝安天皇]]の時代に宇賀野魂命（うかのみたまのみこと。その別称が豊受毘売命）が降臨し、時を同じくして筑摩村に[[御食津神|御食都神（みけつかみ）]]、岩脇村に[[大歳神]]が降臨、この3神を合わせて「筑摩三所の神」と称したといい筑摩神は現[[筑摩神社 (米原市)|筑摩神社]]、岩脇神は現[[稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)|稲荷神社]]。、また鎮座地「宇賀野」は「宇賀野魂」という神名に因んだものであるという『近江坂田郡志』、滋賀県坂田郡役所、大正2年。。その後、[[延喜式神名帳|延喜の制]]で近江国の小社（国幣小社）に列した坂田郡「岡神社」であるとされ岡神社の論社も複数存在するが、明治の『特選神名牒』は当地にを古く岡村という村があった事、「岡」の音は「宇賀」や「受（うけ）」に通う事を徴として当神社を比定する。、後に坂田宮に[[合祀]]されたものであるという『式内社調査報告』所引『明治神社誌料』。。 後に[[建武 (日本)|建武]]の兵乱で兵火に罹ったために[[佐々木秀綱]]によって再建されたものの、[[応仁の乱]]以降も再々兵燹に遭ったために漸次荒廃していったが、[[享保]]18年（[[1733年]]）に時の[[彦根藩|彦根藩主]][[井伊直惟]]の崇敬を受けて再興、社頭も整備されて以降、「坂田神明宮」と称して彦根藩からの厚い保護を受けた。 [[明治]]14年（[[1881年]]）2月1日に[[郷社]]に列し、同41年4月29日に[[神饌幣帛料供進社]]に指定、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）には[[県社]]に昇格した。 現在、境内の一部を分断するようにを[[北陸本線]]が横切っていて最寄り駅も、[[坂田駅]]である。同様に境内を鉄道の線路が横切っている神社に[[澤田八幡神社]]がある。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#別宮|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:近江国の式内社]] [[Category:滋賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:米原市の建築物]] [[Category:米原市の歴史]] {{shinto-stub}}

([[岐阜県]][[下呂市]]／[[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[高山本線]]) * [[関蝉丸神社|関蝉丸神社下社]] - ([[滋賀県]][[大津市]]／[[京阪電気鉄道|京阪]][[京阪京津線|京津線]]) * [[澤田八幡神社]] - ([[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]／[[近鉄南大阪線]]) などが挙げられる（括弧内は所在地と路線名）。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#別宮|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:近江国の式内社]] [[Category:滋賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:米原市の建築物]] [[Category:米原市の歴史]] {{shinto-stub}}

([[岐阜県]][[下呂市]]／[[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[高山本線]]) * [[関蝉丸神社|関蝉丸神社下社]] - ([[滋賀県]][[大津市]]／[[京阪電気鉄道|京阪]][[京阪京津線|京津線]]) * [[澤田八幡神社]] - ([[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]／[[近鉄南大阪線]]) などが挙げられる（括弧内は所在地と路線名）。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#概要|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:近江国の式内社]] [[Category:滋賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:米原市の建築物]] [[Category:米原市の歴史]] {{shinto-stub}}

([[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]／[[近鉄南大阪線]]) * [[陶山神社 (有田町)|陶山神社]] - ([[佐賀県]][[西松浦郡]][[有田町]]/[[九州旅客鉄道|JR]][[佐世保線]]) などが挙げられる（括弧内は所在地と路線名）。 ==祭事== 例祭 - 5月1日 ==境内外社== * 境内社 ** 七所宮（[[皇大神宮|伊勢神宮内宮]]の[[伊勢神宮#概要|7別宮]]に倣ったもの） ** 四所宮（同じく[[豊受大神宮|外宮]]の4別宮に倣ったもの） ** 倭姫社 * 境外社 ** 宇賀野神社 ==文化財== ;重要美術品（国認定） * [[後陽成天皇]]宸翰天照皇大神神号掛軸 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *[[教部省]]撰『[[特選神名牒]]』（復刻版）、[[思文閣出版]]、昭和47年ISBN 4-901339-07-9（初版は[[磯部甲陽堂]]、大正14年刊） *平川昌福「岡神社」（『式内社調査報告』第12巻東山道1、[[皇學館大學|皇學館大學出版部]]、昭和56年刊、所収） *大阪府神社庁編『伊勢の神宮【ヤマトヒメノミコト御巡幸のすべて】』、[[和泉書院]]、平成5年ISBN 4-87088-609-X == 外部リンク == *[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=1038 坂田神明宮]（滋賀県神社庁） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかたしんめいくう}} [[Category:滋賀県の神社]] [[Category:元伊勢]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:近江国の式内社]] [[Category:滋賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:米原市の建築物]] [[Category:米原市の歴史]] {{shinto-stub}}

revision.text:
{{draft|draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] |draft}} {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮|draft}} [[ja:坂田神明宮]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | Name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | Image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | Location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | Coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References == {{reflist}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} == External Links == * According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References == {{reflist}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} == External Links == * It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References == {{reflist}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} == External Links == * The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Shrine | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮}}) * Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) *
