It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** * Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}) * Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** * Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** * Hanging scroll with the It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2年, Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** ** Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇}} == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} * {{ill|Kumano {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled
