It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft|draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] |draft}} {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮|draft|12=draft}} is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** ** Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Sakata Shinmei Shrine]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft|draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] |draft}} {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮|draft|12=draft}} is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft|draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] |draft}} {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮|draft|12=draft}} is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** ** Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|12=draft}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}} == External Links == * Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Sakata Shinmei Shrine]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft}}. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Osaka **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{draft|draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]] |draft}} {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮|draft|12=draft|12=draft}} is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) ** Yamato-hime Shrine * **Off-site Shrine** ** Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * **Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)** ** Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|ja|後陽成天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|draft|12=draft|12=draft}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}} Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=draft|12=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=draft|12=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=draft|12=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=draft|12=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=draft|12=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=draft|12=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|12=draft|12=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|12=draft|12=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=draft|12=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * **festival**: May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * **On-site Shrines** ** Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) ** Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Osaka Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Main hall = {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Maibara|ja|米原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Sakata District, Ōmi Province|ja|坂田郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to the {{ill|Ise Jingū|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', {{ill|Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the {{ill|Kenmu Restoration|ja|建武の新政|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the {{ill|Ōnin War|ja|応仁の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|ja|北陸本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is {{ill|Sakata Station (Shiga)|ja|坂田駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Osaka It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]] Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|qq=}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|qq=}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|qq=}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|qq=}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|qq=}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|qq=}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|qq=}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|qq=}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henshōin|qq=}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|qq=}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishibiki Shrine|qq=}} (Gifu Prefecture, Ōgaki City, served by Seino Railway) * {{ill|Seki-Semimaru Shrine|ja|関蝉丸神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seki-Semimaru Shrine|qq=}} (Shiga Prefecture, Ōtsu City, served by Keihan Keishin Line) * {{ill|Sawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|澤田八幡神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sawada Hachiman Shrine|qq=}} (Osaka Prefecture, Fujiidera City, served by Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line) * {{ill|Sueyama Shrine|ja|陶山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sueyama Shrine|qq=}} (Saga Prefecture, Arita Town, served by JR Sasebo Line) == Festivals == * '''festival''': May 1 == Subsidiary Shrines == * '''On-site Shrines''' ''' Nana-sho-gū (Modeled after the seven auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Kōtai Jingu|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}) ''' Shi-sho-gū (Modeled after the four auxiliary shrines of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|qq=}}) ''' Yamato-hime Shrine * '''Off-site Shrine''' ''' Ugano Shrine == Cultural Properties == * '''Important Artifacts (Nationally Recognized)''' ''' Hanging scroll with the divine name of Amaterasu written by [[:en:Emperor Go-Yōzei|Emperor Go-Yōzei]] == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano faith|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Three Shrines|qq=}} * {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki
