Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]] Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]] Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Other shrines with railway crossings within their grounds include: * {{ill|Henshōin|ja|遍照院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henshōin|1=Henshōin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11640508}} (Kanagawa Prefecture, Yokohama City, served by Keikyū Main Line) * {{ill|Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|ja|下原八幡神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimozuhara Hachiman Shrine|1=Shimohara-hachiman Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11360668}} (Gifu Prefecture, Gero City, served by JR Takayama Line) * {{ill|Ishibiki Shrine|ja|石引神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishibiki Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ It is also a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Motoise shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Sakata Shinmei-gū | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Sakata sinmeigu.JPG|250px]] | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]] Ugano 835-2 | coordinates = {{coord2|35|20|14.6|N|136|17|14.0|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine)
{{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Small Shrine, disputed) - Oka Shrine
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | Established = Traditionally 8th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | Main hall = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shimmei-zukuri]] (Both shrines) | Alternate name = Sakata Shrine | Pilgrimage network = {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} | Annual festival = May 1 | Rituals = }} '''Sakata Shinmei-gū''' (坂田神明宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Maibara, Shiga|Maibara]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]]. It consists of two shrines: the '''Sakata Shrine''' (Inner Shrine) and '''Oka Shrine''' (Outer Shrine). Sakata Shrine is associated with the {{ill|Motoise|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Motoise|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} tradition, while Oka Shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Deities == * {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Sakata Shrine, Inner Shrine) * {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受毘売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-bime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Oka Shrine, Outer Shrine) == Shrine Crest == The shrine crest is a round emblem with a tachibana (Japanese orange). == History == Sakata Shrine, historically referred to as "Sakata Daijingu," was revered as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja (Shinto)]] of [[:en:Sakata District, Shiga|Sakata District, Ōmi Province]]. According to the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingū]] chronicle, the ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}'', [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] moved the deity Amaterasu to Sakata Shrine from "Kōga no Hikumo no Miya" in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, where the deity was enshrined for two years. The shrine traces its origins to the establishment of Sakata Shrine in honor of Yamatohime-no-Mikoto's divine mission. The region later became a {{ill|Mikuriya|ja|御厨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuriya|1=mikuriya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488831}}, or land directly controlled by the Ise Grand Shrine, and its connection to sacred rice paddies dates back to this era.''Ise no Jingū.'' Oka Shrine was historically known as "Oka Tennōsha" or "Wakamiya."{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deguchi Nobutsune|1=Deguchi Nobutsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q108780926}}'s ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyōchō Kōshō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11588824}}''. According to tradition, during the reign of Emperor Kōan, three deities descended in the area: Ugano-tama no Mikoto (also known as Toyouke-bime), Miketsu-kami in Chikuma Village, and Ōtoshi-kami in Iwawaki Village.The Chikuma deity is currently enshrined at {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|ja|筑摩神社 (米原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|1=Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602835}}, and the Iwawaki deity at {{ill|Inari Shrine (Maibara)|ja|稲荷神社 (米原市岩脇)}.} Oka Shrine later became identified as the "Oka Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and its name is believed to be connected to the local village name, Ugano.''Ōmi Sakata District Gazetteer'' (大正2nd year , Sakata District Office). Over time, Oka Shrine was merged with Sakata Shrine. During the [[:en:Kenmu Restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], the shrine suffered damages due to war but was reconstructed by {{ill|Sasaki Hidetsuna|ja|佐々木秀綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Hidetsuna|1=Sasaki Hidetsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11382354}}. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. In 1733, it was restored under the patronage of {{ill|Ii Naochika|ja|井伊直惟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ii Naochika|1=Ii Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11161289}}, the lord of Hikone Domain, who reorganized and expanded the shrine grounds, after which it was officially named Sakata Shinmei-gū. In modern times, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} on February 1, 1881, and elevated to a prefectural shrine in 1945. The shrine grounds are bisected by the [[:en:Hokuriku Main Line|Hokuriku Main Line]], with a railway crossing located on the approach to the shrine. The nearest station is [[:en:Sakata Station (Shiga)|Sakata Station (Shiga)]].
